explanation.text: The Logic: Option spreads are limited-profit and limited-loss positions. They combine a long and short option of the same type — the short leg caps the profit while the long leg limits the loss. The bull-call, bull-put, bear-call, and bear-put examples in the workbook all show bounded payoff ranges. The Trap: Naked options can have unlimited risk (short) or unlimited profit (long), but SPREADS are always bounded on both sides. Note: Spreads are popular because they offer defined risk/reward — you know your max profit and max loss before entering. Source: NISM-Series-I Currency Derivatives workbook, p.101 and pp.103-107.
